definition: How much a material slows light down: the speed of light in air (or a vacuum) divided by its speed in the material. For light going from air into the material, $n = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r}$. It has no unit, and for glass or water it is greater than 1.

The angle of incidence, for light going from a material where it is slower into one where it is faster (such as glass into air), at which the angle of refraction is $90^\circ$. Above it, total internal reflection happens.

When light heading into a material where it would be faster (such as glass into air) meets the boundary at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle, all of it reflects back and none refracts out.
A thin, flexible strand of very clear glass that carries light along it by repeated total internal reflection. Used to send telephone, internet and TV signals, and in endoscopes.
